source: Grace Hill External 30/3/30 Pitch Deck (Bold v6) and Discovery Deck WIP
anchorPromise: Data can show where performance is slipping. Grace Hill gives teams a clear path to resolution.
thirtySecond: Data can show where performance is slipping. Grace Hill gives teams a clear path to resolution. For multifamily teams, that means turning property data, benchmarks, and market context into actions that improve the resident, prospect, and employee experiences behind portfolio results — NOI, revenue, retention, and time to lease.

threeMinute.gap: The gap is not data. It is what happens next. Most teams can see the issue. The harder part is resolving it, getting it done, and proving it worked.
threeMinute.close: Grace Hill is built for the work after the finding. AI is making findings cheaper. It is not making teams less busy. The value is knowing what to do and proving it worked.

marketShift.whatChanged: AI can score more calls, reviews, shops, surveys, and market data.
marketShift.whatDidNot: Your teams still have the same hours and a full day already in front of them.
marketShift.whatItMeans: More findings can become more pressure if nobody knows what to do next.

resolutionLoop.detail: Pull property, lease, resident, team and market context together.
Correlate it to find the cause, not the symptom.
Name the next best action for a specific property.
Put it in the hands of the person who owns it.
Re-measure to confirm the outcome actually moved.

loopNote: Steps 3, 4 and 5 are the ones nobody else does. That's the whole argument. Say ASSIGN, not push-into-your-PMS — deeper two-way write-back is roadmap. Describe assignment to the person who owns the action; do not promise automated write-back into third-party systems.

insight.headline: Residents don't leave over price. They leave over how they were treated.
insight.sub: Which makes your people the biggest controllable lever you have on NOI.

stats.label: Management quality shows up more often than rent increases in stated reasons for not renewing.

rent increase absorbed by satisfied residents, against roughly 3% for the disconnected.

insight.sources: Renewal review analysis across ~79,000 renewals; multifamily reputation index across ~400,000 reviews; published renewal threshold research.
insight.close: Retention is the only lever that raises revenue and lowers cost in the same quarter.

pattern.headline: Four problems. One root cause.
pattern.close: You buy for the symptom. The cause sits upstream.
pattern.ask: Which of the four are you being asked to solve right now?

paysTwice.thisYear: Residents who renew mean fewer turns, less vacancy, fewer concessions. Revenue goes up and turn cost goes down at the same time — the one lever that pays the property manager and the owner in the same quarter.
paysTwice.atExit: Durable NOI capitalizes. A one-time cost cut does not. A structural operating improvement survives the sale — and a buyer pays for it.
paysTwice.arithmetic: $100 of durable NOI per unit per year ÷ a 5% cap rate = $2,000 of asset value per unit = $600,000 on a single 300-unit asset.
paysTwice.note: Cap rate is illustrative. Ask theirs and redo the math live — it lands far harder in their numbers.

alternatives.stops: Records what happened. Won't name the next action.
Four vendors, four contracts. Nothing connects them.
No proven standard underneath. One link, not the chain.
Works in one building. Leaves when they do.

alternativesNote: Be genuinely fair to each option — we lose to all four. Credibility here is what buys you the perfect-world slide. Ask what else is on their shortlist and categorize it into one of these four rather than introducing new names.

perfectWorld.title: One picture
perfectWorld.detail: People, resident experience, and market in one view — not four reports.

perfectWorld.title: A named next action
perfectWorld.detail: Not just what happened. What to do about it, at that property.

perfectWorld.title: One standard
perfectWorld.detail: Holds at every property, not only where a strong manager happens to be.

perfectWorld.title: Proof it worked
perfectWorld.detail: Measured against benchmarks, in numbers your exec team already uses.

perfectWorldNote: This is the hinge of the whole pitch. If they agree with this list, they have agreed to purchase criteria only we meet. Do not move on without an explicit yes.

connectsBothSides.moat: A model can be rebuilt. Years of what happened next cannot.
connectsBothSides.note: Avoid saying 'more data'. Say we connect evidence, context, and improvement on the same properties over time.

ai.changed: Finding problems is becoming nearly free. Any tool can now tell you a property is underperforming, or that a review was negative. Detection is no longer scarce.
ai.unchanged: Knowing the right fix, getting it done, and proving it worked. That needs an owned library of remediations and years of outcomes to compare against — not a better model.
ai.close: More findings just means more to resolve. And whether the person in front of your resident is on payroll or is an agent, someone still has to decide what good looks like.

proofQuote.quote: Grace Hill's products are intentional, helpful, and designed to make our teams better.

objections.objection: We already get some of this free in our PMS.
objections.response: You do — and you should use it. Free modules record activity. They don't benchmark it or tell you which property to fix first.

objections.objection: This is a lot to take on at once.
objections.response: Then don't. Start with one track where the budget already sits. Expansion is a tier change, not a new project.
That's the whole problem — and it's why we priced it so one team can start without waiting on the others.

objections.objection: We're not replacing our system of record.
objections.response: Good — don't. It stays the ledger. We sit above it and hand work back to the people who do it.

Adds AI-generated action plans, full market data, and open API access for your own AI tooling.

tracks.value: Develop people and drive operational consistency.
tracks.loop: Know the gap → Teach the move → Reinforce it → Show progress
tracks.showsUpIn: Training, policies, onboarding, mystery shop results, employee surveys, and role-based learning.

tracks.value: Improve the resident and prospect experience.
tracks.loop: Listen → Prioritize → Close the loop → Improve results
tracks.showsUpIn: Surveys, reputation, benchmarking, feedback and sentiment, response diagnostics, and leasing experience.

packaging.note: Everything priced per unit, per month — so cost scales with the portfolio, not a seat count. Lead with the single track whose budget owner is in the room; combined-track deals have a much longer cycle. Do not quote prices in a discovery meeting.

closingLine: Every team, more effective. Every resident, retained.
